title: Case: Return item identity disputed between merchant and recipient
context: A returned item from a customer should have reached Brineleaf Pantry warehouse but the merchant has no record of its receipt. The customer claims they returned the correct item; Brineleaf says they received a different product. The desk must verify who authorized the return and confirm the item identity before accepting any claim.
initial_request: Resolve a discrepancy between a customer's return shipment and the merchant's receiving records.

events.body: I returned DL-812 (Brineleaf order BL-2894, item Spiced Preserve Jar 500ml, batch 24-A7) on 2026-04-06. Your tracking shows delivered to Brineleaf Pantry Warehouse on 2026-04-08. But Brineleaf say they never got it and I'm being charged for the item. Help.

events.from: Tomas Kuhn, Brineleaf Pantry Returns authorisations
events.body: We have no receiving scan for DL-812 in our warehouse system. Our intake log for 2026-04-08 shows one parcel arrived—DL-813—containing Honey Blend 375ml, not Spiced Preserve. The customer Marta Vex was authorized for a return under case BL-2894-RA, but that was for the Preserve, not Honey. Something is wrong with what was actually shipped back or the tracking.

events.from: Jarl Oswald, staff, Coldmark Pickup Point
events.body: DL-812 picked up 2026-04-06 from customer Marta Vex. Parcel label says Spiced Preserve Jar 500ml going to Brineleaf. It left us that same day. Not our error.
This is ridiculous. I packed the right item. Either your driver swapped it or Brineleaf is lying. I want proof DL-812 was delivered to them and I want my refund NOW or I'm disputing the charge.

acceptable_actions.summary: Request item identity confirmation for DL-812 (what was actually received and logged on 2026-04-08) and reconciliation with DL-813 (Honey Blend received same day) to determine if contents were misidentified or if wrong parcel arrived.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Tomas Kuhn, Brineleaf Pantry Returns authorisations
acceptable_actions.summary: Confirm the return authorization scope for BL-2894-RA and request clarification on why Honey Blend 375ml was received if only Spiced Preserve 500ml was authorized for return.

must: Do not authorize, arrange or recommend any refund or credit to Marta Vex until the item identity discrepancy is resolved.
Send the verification request to Brineleaf Pantry (the owning team and merchant of record), not to the customer or carrier driver.
Acknowledge that tracking shows delivery to Brineleaf but the contents identity is contested and requires merchant intake confirmation.
must_not: Do not accept Marta Vex's claim of correct packing as proof of what was in DL-812 without merchant verification.
Do not contact the carrier Dispatch or driver to investigate the swap allegation before the merchant confirms what item they actually received.
Do not treat the Pickup Point staff's label reading (saying 'Spiced Preserve') as proof of contents; label accuracy is separate from what was packed.
Do not assume DL-812 and DL-813 are unrelated or that one is lost; the merchant received something on 2026-04-08 and must clarify what.
expected.reference_message: To: Tomas Kuhn, Brineleaf Pantry Returns authorisations and Damage intake, Brineleaf Pantry. Subject: DL-812 return item identity confirmation required for BL-2894. Customer Marta Vex initiated return DL-812 on 2026-04-06 (Spiced Preserve Jar 500ml). Your intake log shows receipt on 2026-04-08 of DL-813 (Honey Blend 375ml) but no scan of DL-812. Please confirm: (1) What item was actually unpacked and logged for DL-812 on intake? (2) Is DL-813 a separate customer return or related to BL-2894-RA? (3) Can you reconcile both parcels against the return authorization scope? The customer's refund claim cannot be assessed until Brineleaf confirms receipt contents. Reply with intake photos or scan records if available.

rationale: The customer claims they returned the correct item, but Brineleaf received a different product and has no record of DL-812. The unverified claim from an interested party (Marta Vex) cannot override the merchant's intake records. The desk must ask Brineleaf—the party who received, inspected and logged the return—to verify what was actually in DL-812 and how it relates to DL-813 before any refund or escalation decision is made. Refusing the customer's immediate request without verification is correct; escalating without merchant input would be premature.
